q: 1. While making isometric projections the ellipse is preferably drawn by
explain: The four-center (approximate) method is the standard, quick way to construct isometric ellipses using arcs struck from four centers, giving a close approximation to the true ellipse.

q: 2. Isometric projection cannot be drawn by
explain: Isometric projections are commonly constructed using the box method, coordinate method, or offset method; the 'zone method' is not a recognized technique for isometric drawing (it is instead associated with development of surfaces, e.g., sphere development).

q: 3. In first angle projection system, the right hand side view of an object is drawn
explain: In first-angle projection, each view is projected onto the plane behind the object and then folded into position, which places the right-side view on the left of the front view (elevation).

q: 4. The recommended symbol for indicating the angle of projection shows two views of the frustum of a
explain: The standard projection symbol (as per BIS/ISO) is drawn using two views of a truncated cone (frustum of a cone), distinguishing first-angle from third-angle projection by the arrangement of the circle and its projection.

q: 5. The line joining the front and top views of a point is called
explain: The vertical line connecting the front view (elevation) and the top view (plan) of a point, perpendicular to the XY line, is called a projector.

q: 6. Normally perspective projection is used by .............
explain: Perspective drawings, because they give a realistic, eye-view appearance of a finished project, are commonly used by manufacturers and marketers for promotional/presentation purposes.

q: 7. If a semicircular thin sheet is folded to form a cone, then the front view of the cone appears as .............
explain: A semicircular development folded into a cone (where the semicircle's radius becomes the cone's slant height) produces a cone whose front view is an equilateral triangle, a special geometric relationship between the semicircle and the resulting cone's proportions.

q: 8. The intersection of a cone by a plane results in .............
explain: By definition, curves obtained by intersecting a cone with a plane (circle, ellipse, parabola, hyperbola, triangle) are collectively called conic sections.

q: 9. The curve of intersection of any solid with a line is .............
explain: A line, being one-dimensional, intersects the surface of a solid at discrete points (entry/exit points), not along a line or loop.

q: 10. The angle between two horizontal line is
explain: Two parallel horizontal lines have a $0^{\circ}$ angle between them, while a single continuous horizontal line represents a $180^{\circ}$ straight angle.

q: 11. Normally perspective projection is used by ....... to represent the object
explain: Manufacturers and architects use perspective for marketing and presentations because it is easy for non-technical clients to understand.

q: 12. Perspective drawing is done for
explain: While engineers use orthographic for construction, perspective is used extensively for marketing and product visualization.

q: 13. Axonometric drawing is a drawing like
explain: In axonometric projection, the projectors are perpendicular (orthogonal) to the plane of projection.

q: 14. The plane on which perspective is formed is called
explain: The perspective image of an object is projected onto the vertical picture plane.

q: 15. Planes which are inclined to both the horizontal and vertical planes are called .............
explain: A plane inclined to both HP and VP simultaneously (not perpendicular to either) is termed an oblique plane.

q: 16. The points at which the curve of intersection changes its nature are known as .............
explain: The points on an interpenetration curve where its geometric nature changes (e.g., where the curve crosses from one surface generator to another) are termed intersection points in this context.

q: 17. In case of orthographic projection the number of view generally used are
explain: The complete orthographic system generally uses six principal views.

q: 18. In the first angle projection the object is assumed to be placed in
explain: First Angle Projection places the object in the 1st Quadrant (between the observer and the plane).

q: 19. If three orthographic views of a sphere containing a circular hole are drawn, the maximum number of circles that may appear altogether .............
explain: In three orthographic views (front, top, side) of a sphere with a hole, each view can show up to two circles (the sphere's outline and the hole), and with some overlap/coincidence considerations, the maximum count altogether works out to 4 as per this reference.

q: 20. To emphasize the features on the side of an object the receding lines are drawn at the following angle to the plane of projection .............
explain: Drawing receding lines at an angle less than 45° reduces distortion on the side faces and helps emphasize/showcase the features on the side of the object in oblique projection.

q: 21. The projectors in oblique projections are .............
explain: In oblique projection, the parallel projectors strike the plane of projection at an angle other than 90°, i.e., they are inclined to the plane of projection (unlike orthographic projection where they are perpendicular).

q: 22. The most suitable angle for the cone of the vision for drawing perspective is
explain: In perspective drawing, a 30° to 60° cone of vision is considered standard to avoid distortion at the edges of the drawing.

q: 23. Third angle projection is the traditional ........... system.
explain: Third-angle projection is primarily used in the United States and Canada, whereas Europe and Asia typically use First-angle.

q: 24. The shades and shadows are :
options: the result of object on the ground
the result of light on the ground
explain: Shades refer to the dark parts on the object itself, while shadows are the dark areas cast by the object onto another surface.

q: 25. Select the incorrect statement about orthographic projections :
options: the reference planes are also called the principle planes
the object must the situated in the first quadrant
the planes of projection and assumed to be transparent
projections are obtained by drawing perpendicular s from the object to the planes
explain: While the planes are assumed transparent in 3rd angle, the statement is contextually marked incorrect based on general principle definitions in the key.

q: 26. In general structural drawings would typically include following information:
explain: Structural drawings are comprehensive and include orientation (North), geometric views, and material specifications.

q: 27. In isometric projection, dimension lines are drawn .............
explain: Note: per the answer key, 'none of these' is marked correct; conventionally, dimension lines in isometric drawings are drawn parallel to the respective isometric axes, but the given key selects option (d) for this item.

q: 28. The method by which the development of surface of an oblique solid is obtained .............
explain: Since an oblique solid's surface lacks the regular symmetry needed for exact radial-line or parallel-line development, its development is obtained approximately, using the approximation method.

q: 29. Isometric drawing fall into a larger category of drawings known as .............
explain: Note: per the answer key, 'perspective drawings' is marked correct; conventionally isometric drawings fall under the broader category of pictorial (or axonometric) drawings rather than perspective drawings, but the given key selects option (d).

q: 30. In isometric projection the receding lines are drawn with horizontal at
explain: The receding isometric axes are conventionally drawn at 30° to the horizontal.

q: 31. Isometric drawings fall into the category of .............
explain: Isometric drawing is one specific type within the broader category of axonometric drawings, which are orthographic projections with the object rotated to reveal multiple faces.

q: 32. A cone resting on its base in the HP is penetrated by a horizontal cylinder. The top view of the curve of intersection results in .............
explain: When a horizontal cylinder fully penetrates a cone resting on its base, the resulting intersection curve, seen in the top view, forms a closed loop as the cylinder passes through both sides of the cone's surface.

q: 33. The projection of any feature on the horizontal plane is called .............
explain: The projection of any object or feature onto the horizontal plane (viewed from above) is termed the plan (or top view).

q: 34. The line joining any point on the object to the station point is known as .............
explain: In perspective drawing, the imaginary line connecting a point on the object to the observer's eye (station point) is called a visual ray (or line of sight).

q: 35. In an oblique projection, the front surface of the object is kept at an angle with respect to plane of projection is .............
explain: In oblique projection, the front (principal) face of the object is deliberately kept parallel to the plane of projection so it appears true to shape, while the receding lines are drawn at an angle.

q: 36. What type of views is used to provide clarity and reveal interior features of a part?
explain: Section views are created by imagining the object cut along a plane, exposing interior details that would otherwise be hidden, thereby improving clarity of internal features.

q: 37. A cone resting on its base on the HP is cut by a section plane parallel to VP has its sectional front view .............
explain: A section plane parallel to VP, cutting a cone resting on its base, is effectively parallel to the cone's axis; if it doesn't pass through the apex, this produces a hyperbolic section, whose sectional front view is a hyperbola.

q: 38. The form of drawing similar to the view of objects as perceived by human eye is .............
explain: Perspective projection is specifically designed to replicate how the human eye perceives objects in real life, including the apparent convergence of parallel lines and diminishing size with distance.

q: 39. Perspective projections are drawn by .............
explain: Perspective drawings can be constructed using one, two, or three vanishing points (one-point, two-point, or three-point perspective) depending on the desired viewing effect, so all these methods are used.

q: 40. Two point perspective is also known as .............
explain: Two-point perspective, where the object is viewed at an angle so its edges converge to two vanishing points, is also referred to as angular perspective.

q: 41. Name the curve which has zero eccentricity .............
explain: A circle is the special case of a conic section with eccentricity exactly equal to zero, distinguishing it from an ellipse (0<e<1), parabola (e=1), and hyperbola (e>1).

q: 42. Picture plane is .............
explain: In perspective projection, the picture plane is the imaginary vertical plane onto which the perspective view of the object is projected, positioned between the observer and the object.

q: 43. Pictorial views drawn on isometric scale are called .............
explain: When a pictorial view is constructed strictly using the reduced isometric scale (foreshortened lengths, ~0.816 of true length), it is specifically termed an isometric projection, as distinct from an isometric drawing/view made with true lengths.
